title: Critical Skills Employment Permit for Ireland: a 2-year job offer in a critical skills occupation paying at least €40,904 a year, or any eligible job paying €68,911

sources.title: Employment Permits Act 2024, ss. 2(1) and 7(1): a foreign national, a non-national within the Immigration Act 1999, may be in employment in the State only under an employment permit
Employment Permits Act 2024, s. 8(1)(e): section 7 does not apply to a foreign national entitled to enter and work in the State under the treaties governing the European Union
Immigration Act 1999, s. 1(1): a non-national is an alien under the Aliens Act 1935, other than an alien whom an order under s. 10 of that Act exempts from all of it
Aliens (Exemption) Order 1999 (S.I. No. 97 of 1999), art. 3: every citizen of the United Kingdom is exempted from all the provisions of the Aliens Act 1935
Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment: non-EEA nationals need an employment permit; Swiss nationals work in Ireland without one under the 2001 Act on free movement with Switzerland
Employment Permits Act 2024, ss. 9(2)(a) and 22: the critical skills employment permit for skills in short supply; at least half the employer's staff EEA, Swiss or UK nationals, with exceptions
Employment Permits Regulations 2024 (S.I. No. 444 of 2024), regs. 27 to 29: a relevant degree (or experience above the higher threshold), an offer of at least 2 years and 20 hours a week
S.I. No. 643 of 2025, regs. 2, 4 to 7 and 21 (Schedule 8, Part 1), from 1 March 2026: €40,904 for Schedule 3 jobs, €36,848 for a degree from the last 12 months; €68,911 for other eligible jobs
S.I. No. 213 of 2026, reg. 4, made 13 May 2026: a new Schedule 3, the critical skills occupations, including ICT professionals in SOC 2133 to 2139 such as software developers
S.I. No. 558 of 2026, regs. 6 and 7, made 28 October 2026: Schedule 3 and the ineligible list in Schedule 4 replaced again; ICT professionals in SOC 2133 to 2139 stay on Schedule 3
Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment, Critical Skills Employment Permit: €40,904, €36,848 or €68,911, a 2-year job offer, the 50% rule, immediate family reunification
Policy Document on Non-EEA Family Reunification (12 June 2026), paras. 1.5.1, 6.3 and 10.8: a Critical Skills Employment Permit holder's spouse, partner and minor children may come on arrival
Family Reunification Policy, paras. 7.5 and 7.10: a spouse or civil partner must be 18 or over at application; a recognised civil partnership counts as marriage
Family Reunification Policy, glossary and paras. 7.12 to 7.13: a de facto partner 18 or over, in a relationship akin to marriage with at least 2 years of cohabitation before applying
Family Reunification Policy, paras. 7.21, 7.22, 7.24, 7.26 and 8.2: biological, adopted or step-children, unmarried and under 18; stepchildren must be full-time members of the household
Immigration Service Delivery: amendments to the non-EEA Family Reunification Policy take effect from 12 June 2026
Age of Majority Act 1985, s. 4(1): an age is attained at the start of the birthday anniversary; no Irish rule for a 29 February birthday was found, so 28 February is assumed

requirements.title: Not a citizen of Ireland, another EU or EEA state, Switzerland or the United Kingdom: they work in Ireland without an employment permit

assessments.title: A 2-year job offer of 20+ hours a week from an employer whose staff are at least half EEA, Swiss or UK: €40,904 a year in a critical skills occupation (€36,848 for a recent graduate), else €68,911
A relevant third level degree (a nurse, midwife or radiographer: a degree or diploma their registration board accepts); for a job paying €68,911 or more, a relevant degree or the experience

dependents.title: Spouse or civil partner aged 18 or over
De facto partner aged 18 or over, after 2 years together; a shorter relationship, which may be a civil partnership: possible
Children under 18 and unmarried, biological or adopted; that Irish law recognises an adoption is not checked
The spouse or civil partner's children under 18 and unmarried, as stepchildren; living full time in the household is not checked
